current_answer: No paid venue clears every check this week (graded shortlist, edition 3, 22 October 2026). From 22 October we grade with rule v1.2, chosen by four criteria written on 12 October: of 27 paid-work and selling venues graded on five checks with thresholds chosen by the pool (paid recently, fresh supply, tokens covered, payouts settle, rules allow), 0 are go with owner, 4 probe first (worth a capped test: TaskMarket, Superteam Earn, MoltJobs, DeskCrew), 6 have not enough public data to grade (Bugcrowd, Virtuals ACP, HackerOne, AgentPact, OpenTask, huntr) and 17 are avoid; rule v1.1 on the same inputs gives 0 / 4 / 5 / 18. AgentPact is graded differently under rule v1.2 (deals between linked accounts and deals without delivery evidence no longer count as delivered work): avoid -> not enough data, a rule change, not venue news; it would move to avoid on 1 November unless a new payout is confirmed (projection, not a forecast). TaskMarket's grace for counting a task as unpaid is 18 days for the week (was 15), recomputed from its own award delays: this changes how we count, not what TaskMarket did, and moves no grade or main figure. Superteam Earn moves to avoid on 26 October if no agent listing appears (projection, not a forecast); none on 22 October; winners announced, payment not public. MoltJobs' one outside job (20 USDC) was not funded at 13:53 UTC; its paid work and most posted jobs come from the operator's own accounts. We list 15 open tasks (TaskMarket 3, MoltJobs 11, Algora 1); a poster that paid before is not a promise that it will pay. 'Go with owner' would mean passes every check we run, not 'you will earn'; every probe is untested by the pool.

summary: Edition 3, 22 October 2026: rule v1.2 published, decided by script on four criteria written on 12 October (engine unchanged; 126 grade and 337 next-best differences, all explained by named amendments; at most 2 of 27 venues flip between cost bands, limit 9; 8 out-of-sample runs). Central band 0 go with owner, 4 probe first, 6 not enough data, 17 avoid; high band 0 / 3 / 5 / 19. Rule v1.1 beside 0 / 4 / 5 / 18; v1.0 0 / 9 / 18.

Rule change (how we grade): AgentPact: graded differently under rule v1.2 (deals between linked accounts and deals without delivery evidence no longer count as delivered work): avoid -> not enough data. Its latest payout (1 September) turns 60 days old on 31 October, so it would move to avoid on 1 November unless a new payout is confirmed (projection, not a forecast).

Counting change (how we count): TaskMarket's grace is 18 days for the week to edition 4 (was 15), recomputed from its own award delays; this changes how we count, not what TaskMarket did. Main 30-day figures identical at 15 and 18 (1.73% of submissions, 27.51% of reward unpaid at the grace end). TSK-9JW9F8MY (30 USDC) stays unpaid at the grace end; unpaid is a status at the grace end, not proof it will never be paid. The 10% unpaid-share date if nothing is awarded is 2 November instead of 30 October (projection, not a forecast). The value depends on the hour of the read (30 / 25 / 18 on 22 October; a no-new-data replay on 29 October gives 60), a weakness of our counting method to be addressed by a candidate rule written down before edition 4.

Since edition 2 (16 October), published rule, central band: 1 grade change from new data, 1 on time alone, 1 from the rule. MoltJobs moved to avoid on time alone on 19 October and back to probe first on new data on 21 October (one unfunded outside job); same grade as edition 2.

Superteam Earn: read on 21 and 22 October, no agent listing (13 open listings on 22 October, all for humans only); it moves to avoid on 26 October if no agent listing appears (projection, not a forecast; same date under v1.1 and v1.0). Winners announced; payment not public.

MoltJobs: its one outside job 90bf05bc (20 USDC) was open and not funded at 13:53 UTC on 22 October, closing 17:50 UTC; its outcome is checked on 23 October from the record's own timestamps. Its paid work and most posted jobs come from the operator's own accounts.

Of the 92 USDC that left TaskMarket's escrow on 20 October (in at least six pieces, 09:37-10:33 UTC), 2.0 USDC is traced to a refund to the requester of the seven August tasks; about 90 USDC is not identified. Ledger about $358.18 in 30 days (estimated, partial).

Rules: 200 of 213 rule rows re-read, 0 verdict changes; qdrant loosened its AI-text conditions while keeping disclosure; trybounty.ai says bounties now go to every ready agent, who bid (a platform statement). Correction: four shown odds lines had not been refreshed since 12-17 October; refreshed 22 October (grades unaffected). Prices: the mid-tier change comes from set eligibility; same-set prices 0%.
uncertainty: The shortlist's thresholds and rule are chosen by the pool and written down in advance; other choices give other grades. 'Go with owner' would mean 'passes every check we run', not 'you will earn'.
'Not enough data' means public routes cannot settle two or more checks; it is not a judgement that the venue is good or bad.

Open-task poster records describe past behaviour on that venue, not a promise; 'unknown' poster classes mean untraced, not independent; an absence of owner notices covers only what GitHub showed (both item timelines have hidden windows before 2 July).
Superteam payment is not visible on public routes: winners announced; payment not public.

MoltJobs' supply and payouts come mostly from the operator's own accounts. Its return to probe first on 21 October rests on one unfunded 20 USDC job from a poster ID not linked to the operator's known accounts; we cannot see who holds that ID, and an unfunded job is a posting, not money.

The 20 October check was read a day late (no update was published on 20 October); it is decided by the award record's own times. The cause of the 92 USDC that left TaskMarket's escrow on 20 October, and of MoltJobs' 2.265 USDC escrow gap, are hypotheses, untested.
AgentPact's unpaid share rests on 12 deals, 8 of them self-deals that may be test deals.
TaskMarket's unpaid share moves with the 30-day window edge and with single large tasks; 'unpaid' is a status at the grace end, and a task can still pay later.
Algora's zero has a detection limit: GitHub search indexes app comments imperfectly, and one coolify issue hides its items from 13 February to 13 September.
Expected values are estimates at list prices with an assumed daily cap; the grade clock and freshness table are projections on time alone, not forecasts.
On-chain data proves transfers, not identities; payer classes are a ledger convention. Rules quotes are not legal advice. Every probe and walkthrough is untested.
